newsitem.title: CONGO: Mediation moves in Brazzaville, shooting eases.
newsitem.headline: Mediation moves in Brazzaville, shooting eases.

text.p: Gunfire rang out sporadically across the capital of the former French colony of Congo on Friday but the city was calmer than previously in a bloody nine-day standoff between President Pascal Lissouba and his Marxist military predecessor.

"The ceasefire (call) seems much better respected than yesterday," Bertin Mulunga, a spokesman for Brazzaville mayor and mediator Bernard Kolelas, told Reuters. "It might be early to be certain but it seems to be taking hold."
Mulunga said that a Kolelas mediation committee was looking at possible mediation by Gabon's president, Omar Bongo, and ways of bringing the two rivals together.
Fighting began after the army surrounded ex-president Denis Sassou Nguesso's home as part of a crackdown on private militias and unauthorised arms in the runup to a July 27 election.

Mohamed Sahnoun, the U.N. and Organisation of African Unity special envoy to Congo Brazzaville's huge southern neighbour the Democratic Republic of Congo, told Reuters in Kinshasa that he planned to meet Bongo in Libreville on Friday.
"There's another fire to put out in the region," he said, adding he had been in touch with all sides in the conflict.
